$comment: U18: move CS_R off the west edge (PD10 pin 78 -> PE3 pin 2) and take PD_R off Inner2.
WHY. CS_R exited U1's west edge and crossed the entire package to reach FPC3 at
(250,90): a bottom-layer run at y=103.496 under the crystal/QSPI corner (x 143.8-172.5)
plus 57 mm on top. PE3 is a free full-speed GPIO on the east edge, in the middle of the
right-panel SPI escape group -- the aligned edge. PD_R stays on PD13: its problem was
never the pin but the ROUTE -- 71 mm cut through the Inner2 +5V plane (a diagonal
through the crystal region plus a y=93.5 lane to x=222.8). It inherits CS_R's vacated
corridor instead: same bottom lane, same top lane, clear by construction because the
geometry was DRC-clean under its previous owner.
WHY PD_R DID NOT GET A NEW PIN TOO. The PE3/PE4 escape pocket is fenced by a GND
corner stitch and already holds the three SPI_R vias; exhaustive candidate placement
shows it fits exactly ONE more via (CS_R's, at 162.23,117.92 -- every second position
violates via-via 0.7016 or via-track 0.5286 against V_S/V_M/the MISO horizontal).
North-edge pins (PA0/PA4) are walled in by a +3V3 L at y=97.797 and a GND diagonal.
RESIDUAL, STATED PLAINLY: the y=103.496 bottom crossing under the corner still exists
-- it just belongs to PD_R now. The QSPI_CLK 4-via constraint from plan 002 therefore
remains. The wins are: no net crosses the package west-to-east any more, and the +5V
plane under the right-panel bus is whole again.
CS_R's new east run rides the Bottom layer at y=118.9 (empty, verified by via+track
scan x 161-231) and lands by 45-degree diagonal on a new via at (229.150,103.496) --
the exact start of CS_R's kept tail to FPC3/R47. PD_R leaves the lane at x=210 and
diagonals to y=93.024, joining its kept tail at (223.350,93.024) north of the +5V
diagonal whose (222.1,93.8) endpoint blocks the direct line to the old via.
Schematic half already applied and gated: netlist diff shows exactly /CS_R
-[U1,78] +[U1,2]; ERC 171, zero delta. Firmware note for the carrier code (not yet
written): right-panel chip select is PE3.
REVISION 2, after DRC on the first application (NEW = 4, all mine):
CS_R's join via cannot sit at the tail start (229.150,103.496): a 19 mm GND top
diagonal runs parallel to the tail at 0.494 mm -- legal for the 0.254 track, illegal
for a 0.6 via. The via retreats along the same 45-degree line to (227.5,105.146),
west of the GND segment's endpoint at (228.424,104.920), clearing it by 0.951 mm;
a top jog along the tail line covers the last 2.3 mm at the track-legal 0.494.
PD_R cannot join its tail on the top layer at all. The +5V at FPC3 forms a
continuous wall -- diagonal down to (222.1,93.8), stub to y=93.2, diagonal to
(223.7,91.6), east -- and the tail start (223.350,93.024) sits in a pocket behind
it. That is WHY the original route arrived on Inner2. The fix keeps the old via at
(222.842,93.532) -- a through-via serves the bottom as well as Inner2 did -- and
feeds it from the bottom layer, which is empty here: the descent diagonal now
continues to (220.896,92.6), dives, and hops 2.2 mm on the bottom into the pocket.
The tiny top seg (222.842,93.532)-(223.350,93.024) is likewise kept, not re-drawn.
REVISION 3. The rev-2 retreat via at (227.5,105.146) sat 0.226 mm from the GND
HORIZONTAL at y=104.920 that feeds the diagonal -- the L was only half-mapped. The
corridor into the tail is BELOW that horizontal: the vacated y=103.496 lane east of
x=210, which PD_R no longer occupies. CS_R's bottom diagonal now ends at
(222.23,103.496) -- verified clean on every copper layer at 1.424 mm -- and the last
6.9 mm to the tail start runs on top along the old lane, 1.424 under the GND
horizontal and 0.494 from the diagonal at its closest, both track-legal.
